title: Two Claude Code profiles, and only two
notes: - `~/.claude/rules/claude-profiles.md` rewritten to name both profiles, their
accounts, how each is started and which file each uses; to forbid
`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude` with the reason; to record that an MCP
`command` must be an absolute path; and to mark `gateway-example` as a deliberate
per-profile difference rather than drift, since it belongs to one of the
- `.zshrc` gained `claudeb` beside the existing `claudef`, so both profiles
are named rather than one being "the default". It runs
`env -u CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR claude`: a shell that already ran `claudef`, or
any nested agent session, would otherwise send a bare `claude` to the work
profile without saying so. Nothing in the shell ever set
`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude`, so the stray profile came from an ad-hoc
invocation about a month earlier — plausibly an agent following the old
rule text, which called `~/.claude` "canonical" without saying it is the
result: A third configuration existed at `~/.claude/.claude.json` — one project, one MCP server, and its own `oauthAccount` binding the personal address to the work organization, crossing the email-separation rule in the global guidance. It is reached by setting `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude`, which looks like the way to name the personal profile and is not: Claude Code keeps its config at `$HOME/.claude.json` when the variable is unset and at `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.claude.json` when it is set, so pointing it at `~/.claude` starts a fresh empty profile and every MCP server silently disappears. Parked at a retired-profile directory rather than deleted, because it carries auth. The two real profiles are the personal one (plain `claude`) and the work one (its own `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`).
evidence: both profiles answer with their own account and connect Atrium over MCP after the removal; asked in each profile, both quote the new rule back. `.zshrc` needs a real pty to verify — it returns early for agent shells and again for an interactive shell with no TTY — and under one both functions resolve.
